James L. Dolan is an American businessman.
James L. Dolan is the executive chairman and chief executive officer of Madison Square Garden Sports and Madison Square Garden Entertainment, and executive chairman of MSG Networks.
James L. Dolan oversees all operations within the company as its chairman.
James L. Dolan supervises day-to-day operations of professional sports teams including the New York Knicks and New York Rangers.
James L. Dolan supervises regional sports networks such as MSG Network and MSG Plus.
James L. Dolan was previously CEO of Cablevision, founded by his father.
James L. Dolan's father is Charles Dolan, founder of Cablevision.
James L. Dolan has a nephew named Larry Dolan, who owns the Cleveland Guardians.
James L. Dolan is one of six children of Cablevision founder Charles Dolan and Helen Ann Dolan.
James L. Dolan battled drug and alcohol problems in his early adult life.
James L. Dolan went to drug rehabilitation at Hazelden clinic in Center City, Minnesota in 1993.
James L. Dolan opposed his father's proposed Voom satellite service.
Dolan's opposition to the Voom satellite service was a polarizing controversy among Cablevision's board of directors.
Supporters argued that Voom could propel Cablevision into the future emerging satellite market and a wider customer base.
Opponents, including James Dolan, argued that it was too expensive with no expense relief for the foreseeable future.
The younger Dolan prevailed in his opposition to Voom, leading to its shutdown.
The Voom service's shutdown was an instrumental event in Dolan emerging from his father's shadow as a viable businessman.
James L. Dolan has multiple business failures including purchasing Wiz electronics and entertainment chain which ended up posting losses of $250 million before being liquidated.
James L. Dolan also failed with the Clearview Cinemas chain, which did not generate significant revenue.
James L. Dolan fostered Cablevision's philanthropic partnership with The Lustgarten Foundation.
Charles Dolan and Marc Lustgarten were involved in establishing the Foundation in 1998.
Cablevision made a multi-year commitment to underwrite the Foundation's costs ensuring that 100 percent of every donation goes to researching pancreatic cancer.
Dolan supported MSG's ongoing commitment to the community through the Garden of Dreams Foundation, which partners with MSG to help children facing obstacles throughout the New York metropolitan area.
James L. Dolan played a role in organizing the "12-12-12" benefit concert which raised an initial $50 million for Hurricane Sandy victims.
James L. Dolan organized "The Concert For New York City," generating more than $35 million in aid for 9/11 victims and heroes.
James L. Dolan organized "From The Big Apple to The Big Easy," raising nearly $9 million for Hurricane Katrina relief.

James L. Dolan managed Cablevision's sports properties including the National Basketball Association's New York Knicks, the National Hockey League's New York Rangers, the Women's National Basketball Association's New York Liberty, and the American Hockey League's Hartford Wolf Pack.
The only championship-winning team under his domain is the Wolf Pack who won the Calder Cup in the 1999–2000 AHL season.
James L. Dolan was named as a defendant in a sexual harassment lawsuit submitted by former Knicks executive Anucha Browne-Sanders in 2007.
Browne-Sanders accused Dolan of firing her out of spite after she complained about sexual harassment from Isiah Thomas.
The court ruled in favor of Brown-Sanders and Dolan had to pay $3 million of the $11 million settlement. MSG was responsible for paying the remainder.
James L. Dolan's management of the New York Knicks has been criticized by NBA Commissioner David Stern, who said they are not a model of intelligent management.
The New York Knicks performed abysmally in the early 2000s and have yet to fully recover from this period.
The Knicks did not post another winning season until the 2012–13 season.
The Knicks did not make the playoffs between the 2003–04 and 2010–11 seasons, ending in four-game sweeps each year.
James L. Dolan's management of the New York Rangers saw a decline in performance after winning the Stanley Cup in 1994.
The Rangers failed to make the playoffs from the 1997–98 season until the 2004–05 NHL lockout, despite leading the league in payroll most years.
This was the longest playoff drought in the franchise's history due to questionable and expensive free-agent signings.
Since the resolution of the NHL lockout in 2005, Dolan has allowed Sather to rebuild from the ground up, leading to a revival of the club and organization.
The New York Liberty's president Isiah Thomas was appointed by James L. Dolan on May 5, 2015.
Isiah Thomas' appointment as president of the Liberty was questioned due to his history with the Knicks and the Anucha Browne-Sanders sexual harassment incident.

A sexual assault lawsuit was filed against James L. Dolan in January 2024 by Kellye Croft, a former massage therapist who alleged he pressured her into unwanted sexual intercourse during a tour with The Eagles in 2013.
Croft also alleged that Dolan set her up to be molested by Harvey Weinstein in January 2014.
James L. Dolan rarely speaks with members of the media and communicates through released statements or interviews with MSG Network.
Dolan instituted media training for all Garden employees who might deal with the press under his watch.
Dolan instituted an ironclad rule against team personnel criticizing others in the organization via the media.
MSG implemented controversial media policies limiting access to players, including prohibiting one-on-one interviews and banning writers critical of the organization.
Such measures were not standard practice for other NBA teams.
James L. Dolan lives on Long Island with his wife Kristin, whom he named CEO of AMC Networks in 2023.
Dolan has been married twice and has six sons.
Dolan contributed to Donald Trump's 2020 presidential reelection campaign.
Dolan performs blues-inspired rock as the singer for JD & The Straight Shot, their album was released in March 2019.
